description: The bar chart, titled “Recall@10,” presents an ablation study on the INSPIRED dataset, comparing the performance of four variants of a conversation recommendation system: “Ours,” “-critiquing,” “-scoring,” and “-ranking,” with the vertical axis representing Recall@10 values ranging from 0.1 to 0.4 in increments of 0.1. The “Ours” method, depicted in orange, achieves the highest performance at approximately 0.35, while the three ablated versions—“-critiquing,” “-scoring,” and “-ranking”—are shown in blue and exhibit progressively lower or recovering performance: “-critiquing” reaches about 0.25, “-scoring” drops to roughly 0.12 (the lowest), and “-ranking” recovers to approximately 0.28, placing it between “-critiquing” and “Ours.” The bars are arranged horizontally from left to right in the order listed, with no sorting by value, and visually emphasize the performance degradation when components are removed, particularly highlighting the critical role of the scoring mechanism, whose removal causes the sharpest drop in Recall@10. The chart’s clean layout and distinct color coding effectively contrast the full model against its ablated counterparts, reinforcing the contribution of each component to overall performance.
caption_used: Ablation study on the INSPIRED dataset. The bar chart illustrates Recall@10 values for four methods: 'Ours', '-critiquing', '-scoring', and '-ranking'. 'Ours' achieves the highest Recall@10 value, approximately 0.35, while '-scoring' exhibits the lowest performance at roughly 0.12. Notably, '-ranking' consistently outperforms '-critiquing' with a Recall@10 value of approximately 0.28 compared to '-critiquing's 0.25. The chart highlights a steady decline in performance from 'Ours' to '-scoring', with '-ranking' showing a slight recovery in Recall@10 values. The vertical axis ranges from 0.1 to 0.4, and the bars are color-coded, with 'Ours' in orange and the other methods in blue.
